title: Prompt sockets — idea journal
content:
Quick pitch:

Build a lightweight, composable "prompt sockets" layer that lets product teams attach named prompt fragments and runtime signal hooks to requests. Think: named prompt inputs + runtime bindings (user_profile, recent_messages, system_constraints) that can be swapped without rewriting prompts or code across services.

Why this? (motivation / problem):
- Teams constantly tweak prompts for behavior and cost. Changes are scattered across services, PRs, and SDKs — hard to rollback or A/B.
- Need quick experiments: swap a fragment (e.g., 'concise-mode' vs 'verbose-mode') without a deploy.
- Want to combine behavioral presets + runtime constraints (e.g., token budget, latency tier) at request time.
- Non-engineer product owners want to compose presets without touching model code.

Hypothesis:
- If we provide named prompt fragments + runtime bindings with an API and Console UX, teams will iterate 2–3x faster on prompt tuning and reduce rollout failures because changes are centralized and versioned.

Target users:
- Product engineers building assistant flows
- Platform/SDK teams who need consistent behavior across services
- Solutions / SEs who run customer-facing experiments

Core concepts / vocabulary (working):
- Socket: named attachment point on a request (e.g., "prelude", "reply-style", "safety-guard").
- Fragment: reusable chunk of prompt text or instruction (text or structured template).
- Binding: a runtime value provided to a fragment (user_profile, locale, recent_kv_cache).
- Profile: collection of fragments + default bindings (e.g., "concise-lite-v1").
- Contract: enforcement of runtime constraints (max_tokens, latency_budget, fallback_model).

Rough PRD outline (alpha):
- Goal: Reduce time-to-ship prompt changes; enable safe, observable runtime switching of prompt behavior.
- Non-goal: Replace full feature flag platforms. We only manage prompt/behavior presets and a small set of runtime constraints.

MVP feature set (vertical slice):
1) Basic API: Attach socket names and a profile id to a /generate call. Server resolves fragments and composes final prompt.
   - request param: prompt_sockets: { profile: "concise-lane-v1", overrides: [{socket: "reply-style", fragment: "ultra-brief"}] }
2) Console: list profiles, edit fragments (text area), quick preview (rendered composed prompt).
3) Versioning and rollback: every profile edit creates immutable version id. 1-click revert to previous version.
4) Telemetry: track which profile/version was used per request, tokens consumed, latency, and quality (basic indicator: user_accepted / rejected when available).
5) Simple contract enforcement: per-request max_token and fallback_model. If contract violated, use fallback path and log event.

User stories (informal):
- As a PM, I want to create "brief-mode" that shortens responses, so customer support replies are concise.
- As an engineer, I want to try "brief-mode+strict-billing" for 10% of traffic without a deploy.
- As an SRE, I want to see which profile triggers high latency so we can throttle or change model.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Profile can be created and assigned to requests via API or header.
- Console shows composed prompt preview and version history.
- Requests include profile/version in logs/traces.
- Metric pipeline records tokens/latency per profile.

API sketch (pseudo):
POST /v1/generate
headers: X-Prompt-Sockets: profile=concise-lane-v1;version=3
body: { input: "<user text>", bindings: { locale: "en-US" }, socket_overrides: [{socket: "reply-style", fragment_id: "ultra-brief-v2"}] }

Notes: prefer header for low-friction experiments and SDK param for programmatic control.

Console UX (notes to self):
- Left column: profiles list (searchable). Middle: fragment editor and composed preview. Right: quick telemetry (last 24h requests, tokens, latency) + rollout slider (0–100%).
- Quick experiment flow: duplicate profile -> edit fragment -> set rollout 10% -> watch metrics -> promote.

Telemetry and metrics to capture (initial):
- requests_by_profile_version (counter)
- tokens_by_profile_version (histogram)
- latency_by_profile_version (p50/p95)
- fallback_count_by_profile (counter)
- quality_signal_by_profile (optional: user_accepts/edits)
- rollback_events (audit log)

Experiment matrix (alpha ideas):
- A/B prompt behavior: two profiles, split 50/50, measure user_accept rate and average token cost per accepted response.
- Cost safety gating: if tokens_by_profile over 24h > threshold, auto-throttle rollout. (needs policy work)
- Latency-based routing: if p95 for profile > SLO, route new requests for that profile to cheaper/shorter model.

Sample quick experiments (notes):
- "Support concise": create profile, fragment "reply-style" with 3 bullet guidelines, rollout 5% to support workflow. Track triage time and CSAT.
- "Safety softening": fragment that softens refusal language; pair with manual QA for 1 week.

Implementation considerations / backend: (brainstorm)
- Profile store: small DB table with versioned fragments (immutable version ids).
- Resolution at request time: server loads profile version, renders template, concatenates socket fragments into master prompt. Need to be efficient; cache composed prompts for common binding combinations.
- Caching: composed prompt cache keyed by profile_version + normalized binding keys. TTL short (minutes) because fragments change.
- SDKs: add small header or param; support JS/Go/python. Provide helper to preview composed prompt locally.

Cost/throughput impact:
- Additional CPU for composition negligible if cached. If using many dynamic bindings (large user_profile injection), might increase token size -> token costs.
- Estimate: +1–7% p95 latency for composition if not cached. Need bench on serving runtime.

Risks and mitigations:
- Fragment explosion: teams create too many tiny fragments -> manage with naming conventions and console UX (tags, owners).
- Unintended behavior: centralized fragments change many services at once -> versioning + canary rollout and audit logs to mitigate.
- Security: fragments may contain PII if users paste values into fragments -> console warnings + sanitization + role-based edit perms.

Open questions / decisions: (todo list)
- What is the authoritative renderer for structured fragments (mustache? templating)?
- Should bindings be allowed to inject free text from external sources (risk: prompt injection)? Default to whitelist of binding keys.
- How to represent conditional logic (if locale == xx then ...)? Maybe allow simple scripting later but block in MVP.
- Where should rollout policy live? Console + API or via infra (rollout-service)?

Next steps (short-term):
1) Quick spike: implement profile resolver in a minimal service that composes fragments (2 days).
2) Add SDK header support and a sample integration in support-messages (4 days).
3) Console mockups (Figma) + telemetry plumbing (team: infra + obs) (1 wk).
4) Run pilot with two product teams for 2 weeks.

Notes to self / future bits:
- Consider pairing with Optimize's quantization recommendations: profile could suggest model variant for cost/perf.
- Add 'contract' enforcement to auto-fallback to cheaper model when tokens exceed budget.
- Could be a light-weight way to implement per-customer behavioral SLAs (enterprise).

Random TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Draft Confluence spec and link in linked_artifacts
- [ ] Slack the idea to #platform-product for early feedback
- [ ] Reach out to Mika/SRE for caching/bench numbers
- [ ] Add feature flag scaffold for rollout API

Last raw thought (brain-dump):
I like this as a middle-ground between hard-coded prompts and a full feature flag system — keeps prompt behavior declarative, observable, and reversible. If we keep the surface minimal (profiles, fragments, bindings, contracts) and make it easy to preview, adoption could be fast.

-- Kelsey
